English track only. Pure mechanical recombination, no model call. CAUGHT A REAL FOOTGUN in step_4/PROMPT.md's own literal wording before writing this: the prompt says to combine examples.<lang>.md + qa.<lang>.md 'via pipeline.mdio.markdown_to_chapter() + pipeline.mdio.merge_by_id()' - but mdio.merge_by_id(en, hi) is a CROSS-LANGUAGE merge (fills hi-language fields onto en's own items by matching id) that only ever returns its FIRST argument's own item list; it does not append any item from the second argument that isn't already present in the first by id. Calling merge_by_id(examples_chapter, qa_chapter) here - as the prompt's own wording would suggest - would have silently returned an EMPTY chapter, since examples_chapter (the 'en' argument) has 0 items in this chapter (no Example items exist at all) and qa_chapter's 4 real items (the 'hi' argument, despite also being English) would simply never be copied over, being a disjoint-id same-language pair rather than the same items in two languages. Combined the two item lists by plain concatenation instead (examples' items + qa's items, preserving original order), which is what the two files being 'split from the same source in stage 3' actually calls for - a reunion of disjoint kind-subsets, not an id-keyed field merge. This footgun would recur for ANY future chapter whose own Examples split is empty (or, less obviously, whose examples.<lang>.md happens to have FEWER items than qa.<lang>.md, silently dropping only the excess qa items rather than all of them) - worth flagging to the user as a step_4/PROMPT.md wording risk, not something to silently route around every time. VERIFIED: combined.en.md (4 items) is BYTE-IDENTICAL to 02_extract/chapter.en.md, as expected since nothing was reordered or altered - the two are the same content taken on two different round trips through the container format. tag._parse() confirms balanced containers. Item count sums exactly (0 examples + 4 qa = 4), nothing gained or lost recombining.
